scope.method: Independent reviewer personally viewed every full original page PNG with view_image and read every saved English and Chinese page body, comparing displayed and inline mathematical expressions, hypotheses, ideal notation, and diagram labels/arrows. Enlarged PDF crops were separately viewed to resolve congruence symbols and mixed-case polynomial notation. Embedded extraction and existing translator flags were not accepted as evidence of formula fidelity.

findings.source: The CRT proof prints y1 = 0 (mod product of ideals); the Fermat sentence prints a not-congruent symbol for x, not a mere inequality.
findings.resolution: The equality-sign congruence convention was retained. An enlarged source crop confirmed the three horizontal strokes in x not-congruent 0 (mod p); existing EN/ZH not-equivalent notation was correct.

findings.source: The source prints a = 1 + x p^r (mod p^{r+1} Z), while the earlier EN/ZH drafts silently replaced = with a congruence symbol.
findings.resolution: Restored the printed equality sign in both languages. No mathematical source-error claim was added; this is conventional congruence notation.

findings.source: There are polynomials over a finite field which cannot be identified with polynomial functions in that field.
findings.resolution: Restored 有些 in Chinese to preserve the source's existential qualifier. The English source was already faithful.

findings.source: The source prints cf(x) = sum ca_i X^i with mixed variable case.
findings.resolution: Full original page and enlarged crop were viewed. Both languages now preserve the author's cf(x); the previous Chinese cf(X) replacement and its substantive-error note were removed. The review record was corrected to describe a notation variation.

findings.source: The running text prints the triple (u v,y), omitting the comma after u; the adjacent summation subscript prints (u,v,y).
findings.resolution: Retained the printed tuple in English and confirmed the existing corrected Chinese tuple with explicit visible 译校注.

findings.source: The canonical monoid map phi_0:G→A[G], x→1·x, is asserted to be injective without explicitly excluding the zero coefficient ring, which the chapter permits.
findings.resolution: Kept the original assertion and formulas. Added an adjacent Chinese 译校注: for non-singleton G this assertion needs A≠0; in the zero ring every 1·x is the same zero function. The note states the counterexample without silently changing the source hypothesis.

limitations: This audit verifies faithful correspondence of the saved English transcription and Chinese translation to the scanned source, including explicitly documented editorial notes.
